pad_cell_behavior.source: simulations/OSS_FRAME_GIO.spice -- OSS_FRAME_GIO instantiates one OSS_ESD_5V_DIO(VDD,PAD,VSS,HIZ,OUT) per pad
pad_cell_behavior.HIZ: HIZ=1 (tied VDD) => output driver disabled, pad is Hi-Z / input-only. HIZ=0 (tied VSS) => output driver enabled, pad is actively driven by OUT. Derived from transistor-level trace (MXM9-MXM20), not from a naming guess.
pad_cell_behavior.OUT: data driven onto PAD when HIZ=0 (driver enabled). Irrelevant (don't-care) when HIZ=1.
pad_cell_behavior.note_sda: P13/HIZ13/OUT13 implement SDA as a correct open-drain I2C output: OUT13 is permanently tied to VSS (so the driver, when enabled, only ever pulls SDA LOW, matching I2C's open-drain convention -- SDA is never actively driven high by this device), and HIZ13 is dynamically driven by core.sda_oe. Net wiring shows HIZ13=sda_oe directly (no inverter drawn), which combined with the HIZ polarity above implies core.sda_oe is ACTIVE-LOW as an 'assert drive' signal (sda_oe=0 => actively pull SDA low, sda_oe=1 => release/Hi-Z). This should be cross-checked against the RTL's own intended sda_oe polarity before finalizing -- flagged in open_questions.

_meta.dis_net_resolved: RESOLVED via script/route_gio_core.py (v7's actual routing script, DIS_CHAIN_POINTS/DIS_LINKS): 'DIS' is a real, intentionally-used net -- P7's pad is daisy-chained together with HIZ1, HIZ3, HIZ4, HIZ5, HIZ6, HIZ11, HIZ12, HIZ14 (9 points, one shared net, routed as sequential links purely to save wire, not a directional 'P7 drives' relationship). It is NOT tied to VDD or VSS anywhere -- its logic level is set externally, by whatever the tester/board drives onto pad P7. This was previously an open question (see open_questions_resolved below); it does NOT need a VDD/VSS retie.

chip_top_pins._comment: Chip-level LVS fix (see design_notes.md §82): the top subckt tr_1um_i2c_slave_async previously had NO declared ports on either side -- schematic (script/gen_lvs_spice_top_v9.py's old output, matching the stale pre-v9 src/tr_1um_i2c_slave_async.cir's own '.subckt tr_1um_i2c_slave_async' with no pins) AND layout (src/tr_1um_i2c_slave_async.extracted showed '.SUBCKT tr_1um_i2c_slave_async VSS', only one pin). Neither side exposed the chip's real bond pads as top-level ports, which left KLayout's strict-mode LVS pin/port alignment with nothing solid to anchor on and cascaded into OSS_FRAME_GIO-level pin mismatches (HIZ2/HIZ7/HIZ9/HIZ10/HIZ15/OUT13) seen in src/LVS_error.lvsdb. User-diagnosed root cause and fix instruction: add the 16 real bond-pad ports explicitly to the top subckt on the schematic/SPICE side.

VDD/VSS were already correctly named, so only the 14 data-pad nets needed renaming. This is a pure renaming of already-identical nodes -- no connectivity changed. P9/P10 were floating (NC_-prefixed) nets internally; they still become real top pins because they are real physical pads on the chip regardless of internal usage. chip_top_pin_layout_coords._comment: Physical (x,y) location of each top-level pin marker added to src/tr_1um_i2c_slave_async.gds per chip_top_pins above. Derived from OSS_FRAME_GIO's own PO layer (14,0; tech/TR-1um.lyp comment '# PAD') marker shapes -- 16 of the 20 PO shapes in OSS_FRAME_GIO are 80x80um squares, one per bond pad, centered exactly on that pad's M2 metal (independently verified: every one of the 16 centers falls inside a real M2(20,0) shape when read recursively through the layout hierarchy). The other 4 PO shapes are large VDD/VSS bus-bar markers (2500x45um / 45x2500um at the four chip edges), not per-pad, and were excluded. OSS_FRAME_GIO is instantiated in the top cell at (0,0)/r0/mag1 (pure identity transform, confirmed via klayout.db), so these local PO-layer coordinates equal absolute chip coordinates directly.

open_questions_resolved: [RESOLVED, cross-verified against script/route_gio_core.py] Meaning of the 'DIS' net: it is a real, intentionally-used net -- P7's pad plus 8 HIZ pins (HIZ1, HIZ3, HIZ4, HIZ5, HIZ6, HIZ11, HIZ12, HIZ14), daisy-chained as one shared net purely for wire efficiency (see DIS_CHAIN_POINTS/DIS_LINKS in route_gio_core.py). It is genuinely NOT tied to VDD or VSS anywhere -- its logic level is meant to be set externally (off-chip, via whatever is driven onto pad P7), not baked into this schematic or resolved by a chip-side tie. No action needed; do not retie to VDD/VSS.
